sources.entry: Eradicating non-determinism in tests, Martin Fowler

summary.title: Eradicating Non-Determinism in Tests
summary.one_liner: Learn why flaky (non-deterministic) tests destroy a regression suite, how to quarantine them temporarily, and how to fix the common causes: poor isolation, asynchronous waits, remote services, system clock use, and resource leaks.
keywords: why do tests pass sometimes and fail sometimes
takeaways: Quarantine non-deterministic tests into a separate suite so healthy tests keep giving clear feedback, but fix them quickly and limit how long they stay quarantined.
Keep tests isolated so they can run in any order; rebuilding starting state is often easier to debug than relying on clean-up.
Never use bare sleeps for async responses; use callbacks or polling with a generous overall timeout held in constants.
Replace remote services with test doubles for determinism, and verify the doubles with separate, periodically run contract tests.
Wrap the system clock so tests can inject a fixed time, and use small resource pools to surface leaks early.
summary.summary:
Martin Fowler's article argues that non-deterministic tests, which pass and fail without code changes, make a regression suite useless and can cause developers to ignore failures across the whole suite. He recommends quarantining such tests immediately, with limits on how long they stay there, and then fixing them. The article then walks through the common causes: lack of isolation, asynchronous behavior, remote services, time, and resource leaks, giving a treatment for each with short pseudo-code examples. It is written from Thoughtworks delivery experience.</summary>
